I'm going through the user stories one by one. QUS-001 has a role, an action, and a benefit, so it passes, and the English language is consistent with the rest of the backlog. QUS-002 has a single objective and QUS-003 has no notes, so both pass too. I'm now checking whether the benefit in QUS-004, keeping pages free of clutter, is a real one.

I'm checking the rest of the stories against the same criteria. QUS-005 has no technology named, so it passes. For QUS-006 I'm weighing whether "free of clutter" counts as vague, but the action of deleting campers from the database is clear enough, so I'm marking it as passing. QUS-007 doesn't conflict with the existing CTX-CP-002 rule, so it passes as well.

I'm checking the remaining stories for overlap. CTX-CP-002 covers removing campers who no longer attend, which differs from QUS-006's broader database deletion in its conditions and purpose, so it isn't a duplicate, though it's worth flagging for the analyst. I'm also confirming that QUS-009 uses English like its neighbors, and I'm now weighing whether deleting campers depends on related enrollment records.

I'm checking the INV criteria next. INV-002 holds because keeping pages free of clutter is a clear value for the admin. INV-003 fails: deleting campers from the database leaves open what happens to related enrollments, payments, and history, whether the delete is hard or soft, and whether confirmation is needed, so the story can't be estimated yet.

I'm now checking the INV-004 size, which looks small once the scope is clear, and INV-005, which fails because no acceptance criteria are written. For DOR-001, I'm weighing whether deleting campers reaches into other systems or modules like enrollments or billing, and I'm leaning toward treating it as not applicable since the story doesn't name any such integration.

I'm weighing the deletion's edge cases: related records, confirmation, permissions, and soft versus hard delete are all unspecified, and deleting campers with active enrollments or payments is an implicit validation the story never mentions. So DOR-002 fails, and I'm checking the non-estimation defects, INV-003 and DOR-002 as major and INV-005 as blocking. I'm leaning toward returning the story because the scope isn't clear enough to estimate it.

I'm going to look up reference estimates for a simple camper deletion, since the scope is somewhat clear even if the edge cases aren't. My provisional sense is a 2, to be confirmed against the reference points.
